task:
The router mishandles absolute-form request targets, and query text can choose the route. With routes on '/' and '/admin', find('GET', 'http://localhost?next=/admin', { host: 'localhost' }) selects the /admin handler. Clients can use this to reach a route that the request path does not name.

An http or https target with an empty path must route to '/', and keep its query string. The scheme is case-insensitive. For each of 'http://localhost?next=/admin', 'https://localhost?next=/admin' and 'HTTP://localhost?next=/admin', find must return the '/' handler with searchParams deep equal to { next: '/admin' }.

These pairs must give deep-equal find results, with the same constraints:
'http://localhost?next=//admin/settings&return=/' and '/?next=//admin/settings&return=/'
'http://localhost/?next=/admin' and '/?next=/admin'
'http://localhost' and '/'
'http://localhost:8080/a/100' and '/a/100'
'http://123.123.123.123/a' and '/a'

lookup must behave the same way. lookup({ method: 'GET', url: 'http://example.test?next=/admin', headers: { host: 'example.test' } }, null) must run the '/' handler and pass searchParams { next: '/admin' }. Under a real node:http server with this request target, the '/' handler must run and req.url must stay the original target.

Invalid http targets are bad URLs. 'http:///admin' has no host, 'http://localhost#next=/admin' has a fragment, which an http target must never contain, and 'http://localhost:invalid/admin' has an invalid port. With the onBadUrl option set, find on each one must return a match whose handler, when run by callHandler(match, null, null), calls onBadUrl with the full original url as the first argument. These targets must never select /admin. Without onBadUrl, find returns null, as for other bad URLs.

Targets that do not start with '/' and are not http or https keep their current behavior.

The startup check that throws 'the FULL_PATH_REGEXP is not safe, update this module' must no longer exist. If the safe-regex2 dependency is replaced by a function that always returns false, requiring the module must throw new Error('the OPTIONAL_PARAM_REGEXP is not safe, update this module'). So no earlier pattern check may run.

Everything else must keep working.
